sections.heading: D — Accuracy and verification
sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy and verification

Source: every knowledge fact in parts C and C2 cites exactly one physical page of the private snapshot of the Washington Driver Guide, the issuer's own publication, read from extracted page text.
Confidence: high for the risk, speed, space, merging and time facts, each restated from one explicit sentence or list item; the zipper merge traffic-flow figure is reported as the guide's own claim, not independently confirmed.
Precision rule: the crash-risk age band, the two-vehicle-length gap, the zipper merge figure and the counting-seconds marker are kept exactly as printed inside cited fact blocks in C and C2, with the wording paraphrased so that no learner line copies the guide.
Accuracy flags: the zipper merge traffic-flow improvement figure is reported only as the guide's own claim and was not checked against a traffic study, and the chapter opener page before this range was excluded as a title page (verify — sec12-D-FLAG).
Stability: the guide is a single published revision and states it may lag new legislation, so any rule that a future law changes must be re-read from the current edition before reuse.
External review: no clinical or legal review is required; the content restates published licensing and traffic rules for exam preparation only.

corpus_stability.reason: The Washington Driver Guide is one published guide revision (form line 520-400 R/4/25 on physical p4); the guide itself notes it may lag recent legislative changes, and nothing on the selected pages indicates more than one rewrite per year.

verification_debt.claim_text: Zipper merging 'improves traffic flow by 60 percent' (physical p160) is the guide's statement; no underlying study is cited or checked
